caption: A lightning bolt strikes a lone tree on a golf course, and the tree's trunk splits with a shower of splinters.

sa.check: A lone tree on a golf course.
A lightning bolt strikes the tree.
The bolt ends at the tree, not beside it.
The bolt comes first, the split and splinters follow.

pc.expect: The bolt and flash are brief; the split happens at the flash and remains; the trunk does not glow afterwards and the split does not close.
pc.fail: The bolt stands as a steady lit line for the rest of the clip; or the trunk splits before the bolt arrives; or the split closes and the trunk knits back together; or the trunk glows like an ember for the rest of the clip; or splinters fly back into the trunk.

pc.expect: The trunk splits as wood: it cracks along its length into fibrous pieces that stay stiff; pieces knocked off fly outward as solid fragments.
pc.fail: The trunk bends or folds like rubber; or flows or melts at the strike; or the wood shatters into powder like glass; or the split edges stretch like taffy.

pc.expect: The splinters fly out from the trunk and fall to the ground, arcing downward; loose pieces come to rest on the grass.
pc.fail: Splinters rise and hang in the air; or fall upward; or stop in mid-air; or drift sideways without dropping.

pc.expect: The flash lights the tree, the fairway and the cloud undersides during the bolt.
pc.fail: The bolt is visible while the tree and fairway stay as dark as before; or the fairway lights up while no bolt is present; or the ground is lit far from the tree while the tree's surroundings stay dark.

pc.expect: One tree, split or whole; the pieces that fly off come from the trunk; the course and its features are the same before and after.
pc.fail: The tree vanishes or a second tree appears; or splinters appear in the air from nowhere; or the tree turns into a different object; or the bolt passes through the tree into the ground as a lit line.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The grass, the sky and the tree's foliage keep their colours apart from the flash and the damage.
pc.fail: The grass changes colour; or the sky turns to daylight after the flash; or the foliage changes colour rather than brightness.
